title: Majestic Rook
summary: Keep the h-pawn available as support before giving up the rook and advancing the protected passer.

nodes.question: Should the rook move aside immediately?
nodes.explanation: White has Kf8, Rh6, g5 and h5 against Kh8, Rd4 and h7. Rh6 pins h7 to the king, so g6 can exploit the pin before the rook is exchanged.

branches.title: Exploit the pin, then keep a supporting pawn
commentary: Begin from the complete seven-piece source diagram, including the h-pawns that decide both promotion and stalemate resources.
g6 advances while h7 is pinned to Kh8 by Rh6, so ...hxg6 is illegal here.
Rd7 is the illustrated defense of h7, preparing to recapture the rook.
Rxh7+ removes the pawn with check and offers the white rook.
Rxh7 accepts the rook sacrifice. White’s remaining pawns must now cooperate rather than rush independently.
h6 preserves two separate pawns and prepares a protected g7 advance.
Rc7 is the source’s selected rook retreat, avoiding the mating trap after ...Rxh6.
g7+ advances with check. The pawn is protected by h6, preventing ...Rxg7.
Kh7 leaves the corner, since the checking pawn cannot be captured safely.
g8=Q+ promotes with check. The exact queen-and-pawn versus rook ending is winning; conversion beyond this endpoint is not assumed.
branches.explanation: g8=Q+ promotes with check. The exact queen-and-pawn versus rook ending is winning; conversion beyond this endpoint is not assumed.

branches.title: Black takes the supporting pawn
commentary: Compare the illustrated attempt to remove the h-pawn after accepting White’s rook sacrifice.
g6 exploits the pin on h7.
Rd7 guards the h-pawn and invites the rook trade.
Rxh7+ offers the rook with check.
Rxh7 accepts the offered rook.
h6 prepares g7 with pawn support.
Rxh6 removes that support but puts the rook where it cannot stop promotion with check.
g7+ forces the king away while the pawn approaches promotion.
Kh7 is the only legal king reply; Kf8 controls g7 and g8.
g8=Q# is actual mate. The new queen controls h7 and h8, Kf8 protects the queen, and Rh6 blocks the remaining h6 flight.
branches.explanation: g8=Q# is actual mate. The new queen controls h7 and h8, Kf8 protects the queen, and Rh6 blocks the remaining h6 flight.

branches.title: Move the rook before exploiting the pin
commentary: Compare the source’s natural attempt to clear the pawns’ path by moving the rook first.
Rf6 releases the pin on h7 and gives up White’s exact win.
Rd7 defends the seventh rank against the pawn advance.
g6 no longer has the same force because the h-pawn can capture legally.
hxg6 exchanges Black’s h-pawn for White’s g-pawn.
Rxg6 recaptures, but White now has only a rook and an h-pawn against the rook.
Rg7 is the illustrated blockade. This exact rook-and-h-pawn ending is drawn.
branches.explanation: Rg7 is the illustrated blockade. This exact rook-and-h-pawn ending is drawn.

exercises.prompt: Why does g6 work before Rf6?
exercises.answer: Rh6 pins h7 to Kh8. Moving the rook first releases that pin and allows ...hxg6, leaving the drawn rook-and-h-pawn ending.

exercises.prompt: Why keep the h-pawn instead of rushing g7?
exercises.answer: After the rook sacrifice, h6 protects g7. Black cannot take that pawn with the rook without allowing the checked mating promotion.

startContext: The complete seven-piece source position is visually reconstructed. Three selected source branches compare g6 while h7 is pinned, the supporting h6 move, actual promotion mate after ...Rxh6, and the drawn rook-first route. Every encoded position is checked exactly.
verification_scope: Saved board images reviewed manually. Every encoded intermediate position and endpoint is checked against the tablebase. Selected instructive variations, not an exhaustive tree of all legal defenses.
